sources.entry: TMOP - Task manager and system monitor with CPU, memory, disk and network graphs and process management; also runs on Windows and Linux. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/tekikaito/tmop) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: TMOP
summary.one_liner: TMOP (Task Manager OverPowered) is a free, open-source task manager and system monitor for Windows, Linux and macOS that runs without an installer.
use_cases: Monitor live CPU, memory, disk, network and GPU usage
Find and close a hung program
Replace Windows Task Manager with a more detailed tool
Find what is filling up your disk
Check startup apps, services and installed apps
Manage Docker containers from a desktop tool
summary.what_it_does: TMOP shows live graphs for every processor core, memory, disks, network and the graphics card. It lists running programs and lets you end tasks, and includes pages for services, startup apps, installed apps and drivers, and network connections. It has built-in speed tests for processor, memory and disk, plus a Disk Space view and a flight recorder for later review. A popout window can stay on top of other windows, and on Windows it can optionally replace Task Manager. It is distributed as a single program that starts with a double-click, or via install commands, Homebrew or Scoop.
notable: Open source, built by GitHub Actions from public code, with SHA-256 checksums
Single-file program with no installer; install scripts and Homebrew/Scoop options
Can replace Windows Task Manager via Ctrl+Shift+Esc
Flight recorder and built-in speed tests
caveats: Temperatures and per-engine GPU load are not available on macOS; Apple Silicon Macs report no clock speeds
Popout always-on-top is not available on Linux under Wayland
Mac app is not notarized by Apple, so macOS asks for confirmation on first start; macOS 11 or newer required
